subject: Orionix capacity: model footprints & quantization decisions
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex@orionix.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@orionix.ai>
Date: 2028-05-04T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Orionix — model footprints & quant decisions

Marcus —

Thanks again for the call earlier. To make the upcoming procurement review concrete, sending the model variants and expected traffic patterns so you can recommend a dedicated footprint and any quantization options that make sense. High-level:

- Models: "Orion-Large" (base FP16 ~38B params) and "Orion-Long" (same weights but extended context, up to 64k)
- Typical session: 1.5 prompts / session, avg prompt length 1.2k tokens, output avg 400 tokens
- Peak concurrent sessions expected: 35 (initial), scaling to 150 in Q4 if we commit to reserved capacity
- Desired latency: P95 <= 350ms for interactive generation (8k context), and batched async for 64k context where P95 <= 2.5s is acceptable
- Preferences: prefer quantized weights if latency/cost tradeoff is favorable; cannot compromise model quality beyond ~2% delta on Rouge/F1 for core prompts

Attached: orionix_model_profiles.csv (token distributions and a few sample prompts) and the RFP PDF with procurement timelines. Please reply with: 1) recommended GPU count for a 6-month reserved plan (initial and ramp), 2) headroom/overcommit guidance for 64k contexts, 3) any risks that would affect SLAs or billing.

Appreciate a short decision log we can include in the SOW.

—Alex
Head of ML Ops, Orionix
[Attachment: orionix_model_profiles.csv] [Attachment: orionix-reqs-2028-05.pdf]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex@orionix.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-04T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orionix — model footprints & quant decisions

Alex — thanks for the clear profile and RFP. High level reply below; I attached a sizing workbook (redwood_orionix_sizing_v1.xlsx) with the math. TL;DR recommendations up front:

- Start: 10 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs for the first 6 months, with burst pool of 6 GPUs for spikes.
- Q4 target: 40 reserved GPUs (based on projected 150 concurrent sessions).
- For 8k-context interactive traffic: FP16 gives best latency but int8 quantization (post-training static quant) looks viable for Orion-Large with ~<1% quality delta on your test prompts — reduces VRAM by ~30% and increases packing density. Recommend int8 for production interactive if you accept that delta.
- For 64k long-context workloads: use mixed strategy — keep FP16 model variants for tail latency sensitive streams, and deploy an int8-quantized offload path that shards KV cache to NVMe for lower-cost background workloads. This reduces required GPU headroom by ~25% versus keeping everything in GPU RAM.

Notes and risks:
- KV cache: your 64k sessions generate large KV working sets. We estimate per-session KV footprint (FP16) ~26GB; int8 reduces that to ~18GB. With 35 concurrent sessions, GPU RAM becomes the gating factor unless we enable prefix/KV sharing and offload.
- Offload latencies: NVMe offload adds jitter; for async batch jobs that's acceptable, but it will violate your interactive P95 target if used without a hot-path cache on GPU.
- Throughput vs latency tradeoffs: More batching lowers cost but increases P95; our sizing workbook includes scenarios at 64k tokens/session vs 8k.

Next steps we propose:
1) Internal eval: Redwood to run a 48-hour benchmark on a snapshot of your prompts for both FP16 and int8 variants to measure real quality delta and latency distributions.
2) Deliver a decision log and SOW draft that ties reserved quantities to QPS/SLA tiers.
3) Pilot: 2-week pilot with 4 reserved GPUs + 2 burst to validate production traffic.

I've CC'd Karthik for procurement/SOW and Mina for billing cadence.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_orionix_sizing_v1.xlsx]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex@orionix.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-05T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orionix — model footprints & quant decisions

Marcus / team — quick technical addendum from infra:

- Memory math we used in the workbook (summarized):
  - Orion-Large FP16 weights in GPU RAM: ~38GB; int8 quant ~26GB (weights only).
  - Per-session KV (8k context interacting): FP16 ~1.6GB/session; 64k context ~26GB/session (as Marcus noted).
  - CUDA workspace and headroom: reserve additional 15% of aggregate VRAM for kernels and scheduler (this is non-negotiable).

- Headroom recommendation: for interactive pool we size for 1.6x peak concurrent sessions (to allow for short spikes + scheduling jitter). For your 35 initial concurrencies that means planning for ~56 logical session capacity across 10 GPUs. With int8 packing we hit that; with FP16 only you'd need ~14-16 GPUs.

- KV offload strategy: we prefer a tiered cache: hot KV stays on GPU for last-N tokens (configurable window ~8k), warm KV moves to NVMe SSD, cold archived to object store. That requires an IO-aware runtime; we'll include recommended NVMe specs in the benchmark plan.

- Quantization caveats: int8 inference is stable for forward generation for this architecture but watch for distributional drift on long-context retrieval prompts; we will include a regression harness in the 48-hour bench.

I'll own the benchmark; Marcus I'll ping you with expected infra times and the nvme SKU suggestions.

—Soojin
Senior ML Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — this is exactly what procurement needs. Quick replies:

- We accept the proposed pilot (4 reserved + 2 burst) and the 48-hour bench. Please send a SOW that ties the reserved increments to the QPS tiers; procurement target is to sign a 6-month reserved contract with quarterly checkpoints.
- We are comfortable with int8 for the 8k interactive path if the 48-hour bench confirms <1.5% aggregate quality delta across the core prompts.
- For 64k workloads we prefer the mixed approach you outlined — keep a small FP16 hot pool for latency-sensitive sessions and use int8+NVMe for background batch processing.

Action items for Redwood: SOW draft, bench schedule, and an initial PO-eligible invoice line item so procurement can draft the PO. Karthik / Mina — can you own SOW/invoice?

I'll loop Sara (procurement) once we have the SOW. Thanks again — looking forward to the bench results.
